Form 8859 is also a limb of /isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB, so the filer whose only Worksheet-B credit is Form 8859 is detected. Fact.Name: Bona fide resident of Puerto Rico (intake)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's own attestation that they were a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico for the tax year, within the meaning of section 937(a). THE INTAKE HALF of the trio idiom: an optional Writable that NO shipping fact reads directly. Everything downstream reads the complete-safe alias /isBonaFidePuertoRicoResident, because a bare unanswered Writable inside the Schedule 8812 Part II-B routing would take /maximumActc Incomplete by contagion for every filer in the corpus — the /aotcMagi failure class.
SELF-REPORTED, and that is not a shortcut. The instructions give the taxpayer the test to apply and do not derive it from anything on the return: "Generally, you were a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico if, during 2025, you: Met the presence test, Did not have a tax home outside of Puerto Rico, and Did not have a closer connection to the United States or to a foreign country than you have to Puerto Rico." None of those three is a modeled input.
NOT the same fact as a PUERTO RICO SOURCE INCOME amount. Residency is a status Schedule 8812 Part II-B reads on its own; the section 933 exclusion dollar is not built here; this path would be its eligibility input.

Fact.Name: Filer is a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico (Schedule 8812 Part II-B)
Fact.Description:
Whether the filer was a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico, as the Schedule 8812 Part II-B routing needs it. THE COMPLETE-SAFE ALIAS half of the trio idiom: the IsComplete/Switch resolves FALSE when the attestation is unanswered, which is today's behaviour exactly, so no existing return moves. /maximumActc and /pdf8812ContinueFromLine20 read THIS path, never the writable.
WHAT IT CHANGES. Part II-B is headed "Certain Filers Who Have Three or More Qualifying Children and Bona Fide Residents of Puerto Rico", and the line-20 routing note sends a PR resident there regardless of the three-child test: "No. If you are a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico, go to line 21." The statute is explicit — section 24(k)(2)(B)(ii) provides that for a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico "subsection (d)(1)(B)(ii) shall be applied without regard to the phrase 'in the case of a taxpayer with 3 or more qualifying children'" — and the instructions say the same in plain words: "If you were a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico, you may be eligible to claim the ACTC if you had at least one qualifying child." Before this fact, /maximumActc gated strictly on /threeOrMoreCtcEligibleDependents and /pdf8812ContinueFromLine20 implemented only the U.S. line structure, so a PR-resident return with one or two qualifying children was silently computed on the U.S. path and UNDER-claimed.
WHAT IS NOT COMPUTED, AND HOW EACH PART IS HANDLED. Answering this attestation true routes a filer with fewer than three qualifying children into Part II-B, where the instructions add two Puerto Rico legs. • LINE 21 must "include all your withheld social security, Medicare, and Additional Medicare taxes, including those taxes withheld by Puerto Rican employers that are shown on Puerto Rico Form(s) 499R-2/W-2PR". /sched8812Line21 reads Form W-2 only. A return with a child tax credit qualifying child and a Form 499R-2/W-2PR showing box 21 or box 23 above zero is refused by /knockoutSched8812Line21PuertoRicoWithholdingNotIncluded: a short line 21 under-claims the ACTC through Part II-B and over-claims the nonrefundable credit through Credit Limit Worksheet B line 7 (/sched8812CreditLimitWorksheetBLine11 reuses /socialSecurityOverEitc). • LINE 18a must exclude "income earned in Puerto Rico, which you exclude from U.S. tax as a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico". Wages on a Form 499R-2/W-2PR reach none of the three addends of income:/earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay (Form W-2 wages, formW2s:/allCombatPay and scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax), so there is nothing to exclude. Excluded Puerto Rico Schedule C profit is kept out by the third addend, which follows IRC 24(d)(1)(B)(i)'s "which is taken into account in computing taxable income". Section 933(1) exempts a bona fide resident's "income derived from sources within Puerto Rico (except amounts received for services performed as an employee of the United States or any agency thereof)" (26 U.S.C. 933, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section933&num=0&edition=2024, the left column of a two-column extraction); a filer who enters that exclusion on Schedule 8812 line 2a (/writablePuertoRicoIncomeExclusion933) is refused by /knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion, witnessed at tests/nodes/ty2025/ctcOdc/sched8812-magi-three-exclusion-terms. That refusal reaches the filer who is asked and answers: line 2a is an optional Writable, the intake posture every complete-safe alias in this module rests on.
A THIRD SCOPE FACT, stated so it is not mistaken for a gap: a bona fide PR resident who is not required to file Form 1040 or 1040-SR claims the ACTC on Form 1040-SS instead of Schedule 8812. Form 1040-SS is outside this repo's federal-1040 scope (invariant #7) and is not a missing fact.

Fact.Name: Continue Schedule 8812 from Line 20
Fact.Description:
Whether to continue in sequence from Line 20.
THE PUERTO RICO ARM, added with /isBonaFidePuertoRicoResident. The line-20 routing note has two branches and the first of them is conditional on residency, which this fact previously collapsed to an unconditional "skip Part II-B". Line 16b under $5,100 reads: "No. If you are a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico, go to line 21. Otherwise, skip Part II-B and enter the smaller of line 17 or line 20 on line 27." So the first Case's Then is the residency alias, not a bare False — TRUE for a PR resident, FALSE for everyone else, which is byte-for-byte today's behaviour when the attestation is unanswered.
THE $5,100 BRANCH IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. When line 16b is $5,100 or more the note reads "Yes. If line 20 is equal to or more than line 17, skip Part II-B ... Otherwise, go to line 21" — no residency condition at all, so the PR arm must not reach into it. That is why the residency alias appears in the FIRST Case only, and tests/nodes/ty2025/ctcOdc/pr-resident-three-qc-line16b-boundary pins the boundary: at line 16b = $5,100 exactly the Yes branch owns the routing and the attestation changes nothing.
⚠ THE PR ARM ON THIS FACT IS SOURCE-DERIVED BUT NOT WITNESSED BY A NODE TEST, and saying so is cheaper than a green that means nothing. The arm sits in the first Case, whose input /pdf8812Line16bAmount is a PDF-display fact that is undefined unless /pdf8812ContinueFromLine16a (i.e. /remainingCtcAndOdc != 0) resolves — and no ctcOdc fixture on disk makes /remainingCtcAndOdc resolve at all, so in every node test the first Case is skipped and this fact falls through to its unconditional True. The three PR cases assert that fallthrough to guard it against regression, and their transcripts say plainly that it is the fallthrough. Closing this needs a ctcOdc fixture that completes the Part II-A display chain, which is a fixture gap, not a tax-logic one.
THE SCOPE OF THAT GAP IS DISPLAY-ONLY, and it is bounded by reading the consumers rather than by hoping. Every fact that depends on this one is a Schedule 8812 PDF display fact — /pdf8812Line24, /pdf8812Line25 and /pdf8812Line26, each "undefined otherwise". The CREDIT chain does not pass through here at all: /maximumActc reads /threeOrMoreCtcEligibleDependents, /isBonaFidePuertoRicoResident, /regularMaximumActc and /socialSecurityOverEitc, and /additionalCtc reads /maximumActc and /remainingPotentialActc. So the unwitnessed arm can mis-route a PRINTED Part II-B, never a dollar of tax — and the dollar arm of this change, /maximumActc, IS witnessed (318 with the attestation answered true against 252 unanswered, on one fixture where nothing else differs).

Fact.Name: i1040s8 Additional Medicare Tax and RRTA Tax Worksheet, line 8 (Tier 1 tax, box 14)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 8, "Enter the Tier 1 tax (Form(s) W-2, box 14)": the sum of formW2s:/formW2s/*/tier1RrtaTaxUnrounded over EVERY W-2 on the return, cents preserved.
RETURN-LEVEL, NOT PER-FILER, and that is the shape the worksheet has. Its lines 1 and 2 read "Form(s) W-2, box 4" and "box 6" with no filer split, and this fact's neighbour for those lines (formW2s:/socialSecurityTaxesWithheld) sums the whole /formW2s collection including a spouse's W-2s. Schedule 8812 line 21 is a single return-level entry, so a per-filer split here would have no line to land on. Contrast Schedule 3 line 11, which the instruction explicitly says to "figure separately for you and your spouse" because section 3101 caps that credit per person — a distinction the two computations must keep.
CENTS PRESERVED, ROUNDED ONCE AT LINE 21. Box-14 amounts carry cents, and i1040gi page 23 governs a line built by addition: "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total". /sched8812Line21 is where the single Round sits.
THE FLUSH-TEXT EXCLUSION IS STRUCTURAL HERE. "Do not include amounts in Form W-2, box 14, that are identified as Additional Medicare Tax or Tier 2 tax." This fact reads only ../TIER_1_TAX, and ../TIER_2_TAX and ../ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX are separate per-code fields with their own consumers, so there is nothing to exclude — the intake shape enforces it rather than a subtraction. See formW2s:/formW2s/*/rrtaMedicareTaxUnrounded for the printed labelling rule that makes the per-code model the faithful one.

Fact.Name: i1040s8 Additional Medicare Tax and RRTA Tax Worksheet, line 11 (the railroad-EMPLOYEE tier-1 total)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet line 11, "Add lines 8, 9, and 10" — the railroad-EMPLOYEE half of the worksheet's tier-1 section. Line 8 is box-14 Tier 1 tax, line 9 is box-14 Medicare tax, and line 10 is "the Additional Medicare Tax, if any, on RRTA compensation as an employee (Form 8959, line 17)", which this dictionary computes as form8959:/additionalMedicareTaxOnRrtaCompensation. Added into /sched8812Line21's worksheet line 16, alongside lines 6 and 7.
THE DIRECTION OF THE ZERO THIS CLOSES: line 11 is an ADDED term of an ADDED line, so omitting it UNDER-stated Schedule 8812 line 21, under-stated line 23 and so UNDER-claimed the Part II-B additional child tax credit. Taxpayer-ADVERSE, never a false allowance — which is why the two box-14 RRTA submission knockouts that contain this population are the kinder answer until it is modelled, and why this change is a prerequisite of their retirement rather than a consequence of it. Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/ctcOdc/sched8812line21-rrta-tier1-legs-railroad-employee, where a single railroad W-2 moves line 21 from $0 to $14,993.
LINE 10 IS NOT DOUBLE-COUNTED WITH LINE 14, and the worksheet says so twice: line 10 carries "Do not use the same amount from Form 8959, line 17, for both this line 10 and line 14", and line 14 carries the mirror sentence. The instruction is MOOT in this dictionary today because lines 12-15 are a structural zero (no Form CT-2 intake exists — see the scope gap on /sched8812Line21), but it is recorded rather than dropped: the moment a CT-2 surface is built, whoever builds it inherits an anti-double-count rule that is already printed and already read.
WHY WKSHT LINE 10 IS ADDED HERE RATHER THAN INSIDE THE LINE-16 SUM DIRECTLY: the worksheet declares line 11 as its own numbered line and Schedule 8812's own instruction sums "lines 6, 7, 11, and 15", so a fact standing for line 11 keeps the shipped graph readable against the printed page (the round-at-the-printed-line convention). No rounding happens here — the single Round is at /sched8812Line21, the printed entry line.

One Round, here, at the printed line (line 11 can carry cents).

Fact.Name: The filer is directed to complete Schedule 8812 Credit Limit Worksheet B
Fact.Description:
Credit Limit Worksheet A line 3's three-part trigger, verbatim: "Complete Credit Limit Worksheet B only if you meet all the following. 1. You are claiming one or more of the following credits. a. Mortgage interest credit, Form 8396. b. Adoption credit, Form 8839. c. Residential clean energy credit, Form 5695, Part I. d. District of Columbia first-time homebuyer credit, Form 8859. 2. You are not filing Form 2555. 3. Line 4 of Schedule 8812 is more than zero" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 4).
THIS FACT IS INPUT-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. It is the When of every public bridge-credit selector added in steps 2-4, so anything it reads is upstream of those credits. Building it from credit VALUES — "is the mortgage interest credit greater than zero" — would make the selector depend on the very quantity it selects, and the resolver builds EVERY Switch branch eagerly (Switch.scala lines 24-37 via CompNode.scala lines 153-166, no by-name and no Thunk), so a cycle through an untaken branch parks the dictionary load at 0% CPU rather than raising. The three conjuncts are therefore: the three modeled credits' own INPUT gates (each is an Any of IsComplete over that module's writables, plus, on Form 8839, the filing-status eligibility test), the Form 2555 representability gate, and a Count over /familyAndHousehold. Not one of them touches /totalCtcAndOdc, /sched8812CreditLimit or Schedule 3 lines 5a/6c/6g.
COMPLETENESS IS THE THIRD SILENT-FAILURE MODE and it is answered here rather than left to chance. If this fact could resolve Incomplete, every public bridge-credit Switch would have no true Case, and /sched3Line6g, /sched3Line6c, /sched3Line5a, /line8OfSchedule3 and total tax would go Incomplete on all 938 corpus cases — a corpus-wide diff that the empty-Worksheet-B-population argument does not protect against, because it is about completeness rather than value. "CLAIMING" IS READ AS THE MODULE'S OWN IS-ACTIVE GATE, which is the narrowest defensible reading available: form8839:/adoptionCreditIsActive additionally excludes a barred married-filing-separately filer, whose Schedule 3 line 6c is $0, so treating them as not claiming the credit agrees with the amount the return actually carries. Fact.Name: Credit Limit Worksheet B line 6 — the social-security method applies (lines 7-11 are computed)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet B line 6's routing test, which decides whether lines 7 through 10 are computed or left blank with -0- on line 11: "On line 2 of this worksheet, is the amount $5,100 or more? No. If you are a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico and line 5 above is less than line 1 above, go to line 7. Otherwise, leave lines 7 through 10 blank, enter -0- on line 11, and go to line 12. Yes. If line 5 above is equal to or more than line 1 above, leave lines 7 through 10 blank, enter -0- on line 11, and go to line 12. Otherwise, go to line 7" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 5).
Both branches share the "line 5 is less than line 1" condition and differ only in the other conjunct, so the two collapse to ONE expression without loss: line 5 < line 1 AND ( line 2 >= $5,100 OR bona fide resident of Puerto Rico ). The $5,100 is written as 3 x /maxActcAmount rather than a literal, the same idiom /pdf8812ContinueFromLine20 uses for the identical Schedule 8812 line-20 test.
THE "LINE 5 >= LINE 1" HALF IS PROVABLY VALUE-NEUTRAL FOR LINE 14, AND IS BUILT ANYWAY. Suppose line 5 >= line 1. Gated, line 11 is 0, so line 12 = line 5 and line 13 = min(line 2, line 5). Ungated, line 12 = max(line 5, line 11) and line 13 = min(line 2, line 12). Two cases: if line 2 >= line 1 then both line 13 values are >= line 1, so line 14 = 0 either way; if line 2 < line 1 then line 2 < line 1 <= line 5 <= line 12, so both line 13 values are line 2 and line 14 is line 1 - line 2 either way. The gate is written because it is the printed rule, not because line 14 needs it — but the OTHER half of the test is NOT neutral: when line 2 is under $5,100 and the filer is not a bona fide Puerto Rico resident, line 11 is forced to -0- even where the social-security computation would exceed line 5, and dropping that would understate line 13 and overstate line 14.
NOT THE SAME TEST AS /pdf8812ContinueFromLine20, which routes the printed Schedule 8812: that fact's second Case compares line 20 to line 17 (itself capped by line 16a), where this one compares line 5 to line 1. The 16a cap is precisely what Worksheet B omits. TYPE: Boolean; no sign or rounding.

Fact.Name: Credit Limit Worksheet B line 11 (social security taxes in excess of the refundable credits)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet B line 11 = "Subtract line 10 from line 9. If the result is zero or less, enter -0-", where line 9 = lines 7 + 8 and line 10 = Form 1040 line 27a + Schedule 3 line 11 — GATED by the line-6 routing note, which leaves lines 7 through 10 blank and enters -0- here for a filer the note sends straight to line 12.
LINES 7 THROUGH 11 ARE ALREADY ONE SHIPPING FACT. /socialSecurityOverEitc is Schedule 8812 line 25, and Worksheet B lines 7-11 are Schedule 8812 lines 21-25 term for term: line 7 = line 21 (/sched8812Line21, the i1040s8 Additional Medicare Tax and RRTA Tax Worksheet), line 8 = line 22 (Schedule 1 line 15 plus the three Schedule 2 terms), line 9 = line 23, line 10 = line 24 (the earned income credit plus Schedule 3 line 11, whose excess-OASDI half is schedule3:/excessSocialSecurityTaxWithheld), line 11 = line 25. Because this fact reads /socialSecurityOverEitc itself rather than re-deriving line 22, one wiring keeps BOTH directions correct at once: the Part II-B path, where a short line 22 would UNDER-claim the ACTC, and this credit-ordering path, where the same missing dollars would run the other way (line 8 short, so line 14 HIGH, so each bridge credit's limit LOW, so line 15 low, so /sched8812CreditLimit HIGH, so the nonrefundable CTC/ODC OVER-claimed). The Form 8859 line-6h term is a separate, already-closed gap.
THE GATE HAS NO PART II-B COUNTERPART, which is why it is a new fact rather than a reuse of /maximumActc. Schedule 8812 routes the same question at line 20's "Next" note by SKIPPING Part II-B, and /maximumActc encodes that as a Switch on three-or-more-children OR Puerto Rico residency — without the "line 20 is equal to or more than line 17" conjunct, which /additionalCtc's outer min(line 17, line 26) makes value-neutral there. Worksheet B has no such outer minimum, so its line-6 conjunct is carried explicitly here. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (the "-0-" floor is inside /socialSecurityOverEitc); whole dollars, already rounded at that fact.

Fact.Name: Credit Limit Worksheet B line 12 (the larger of line 5 or line 11)
Fact.Description:

This is the same comparison Schedule 8812 line 26 makes, but on the GATED line 11 rather than on /socialSecurityOverEitc directly, and with no Puerto-Rico / three-children Switch around it — the routing lives in line 6 and is already inside line 11. Reading /maximumActc here instead would be wrong on a filer with fewer than three qualifying children who IS a bona fide Puerto Rico resident only in the sense that /maximumActc's Switch also covers the line-17 comparison Worksheet B does not make. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (both operands are); whole dollars, already rounded at both operands.

Fact.Name: Credit Limit Worksheet B line 13 (the smaller of line 2 or line 12)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet B line 13 = "Enter the smaller of line 2 or line 12", where line 2 is the qualifying-child count times $1,700 (/totalPotentialActc, Schedule 8812 line 16b).
⚠ THE SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING LINE IN THIS BUILD, and the one place a careless build reintroduces the fixed point. Schedule 8812 line 27 looks like this line and is not: it is the smaller of line 17 or line 26, and line 17 = min(line 16a, line 16b) where line 16a = line 12 - line 14, i.e. it is capped by the nonrefundable CTC ACTUALLY ALLOWED. Worksheet B line 13 has NO such cap. That is deliberate on the IRS's part — Worksheet B is computing the additional child tax credit the filer could take IGNORING the nonrefundable limit, so that line 14 (line 1 minus line 13) measures the part of the child tax credit that can only ever be used nonrefundably, a quantity that does not depend on the nonrefundable credit. Substituting /remainingPotentialActc (Schedule 8812 line 17) here would make line 14 depend on /totalCtcAndOdc, hence on /sched8812CreditLimit, which after step 5 depends back on line 14 — and the resolver constructs every Switch branch eagerly, so that cycle parks the dictionary load at 0% CPU instead of raising. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (both operands are); whole dollars, already rounded at both operands.

Fact.Name: Credit Limit Worksheet B line 14 (the CTC term the four bridge credits substitute for Form 1040 line 19)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet B line 14 = "Is the amount on line 13 of this worksheet more than the amount on line 1? No. Subtract line 13 from line 1. Enter the result. Yes. Enter -0-" — i.e. max(0, line 1 - line 13), where line 1 is Schedule 8812 line 12 (/dependentCreditLessPhaseout, the dependent credits after phaseout) and line 13 is the uncapped smaller-of above.
WHAT THIS NUMBER IS, in one sentence, because the path name under-advertises it: line 13 is the additional child tax credit the filer could take ignoring the nonrefundable limit, so line 14 is the part of the total child tax credit that can ONLY be taken nonrefundably — and that is exactly the amount Form 8396, Form 8839, Form 5695 Part I and Form 8859 must treat as already applied against tax when they figure their own limits. The i5695 and i8839 worksheets say so in the same words: "include the amount in the instructions for Schedule 8812 (Form 1040), Credit Limit Worksheet B, line 14, INSTEAD OF the amount from Form 1040 ... line 19" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i5695.pdf, page 5; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8839.pdf, page 7). Because it depends on none of those four credits, substituting it for Form 1040 line 19 is what makes the whole ordering acyclic.
NOT YET READ BY ANYTHING at this step — the twins that consume it land in steps 2 through 4 and Credit Limit Worksheet A line 4 in step 5, so this commit is purely additive. It is exported downstream so the wiring lint sees a live surface rather than an orphan.
THE ELIGIBILITY GATES ON LINES 1 AND 2 AGREE, so line 14 lands somewhere defensible on a disqualified return rather than by accident. /totalPotentialActc (line 2) returns $0 when /ctcOdcDisqualifiedForImproperClaims or Not(/maybeEligibleForCtc), and /dependentCreditLessPhaseout (line 1) inherits the SAME improper-claims gate through /totalPotentialCtc and /totalPotentialOdc. So a filer disqualified for improper claims has line 1 = line 2 = 0 and line 14 = 0, and a filer eligible for the credit for other dependents but not the child tax credit has line 2 = 0 (no qualifying children to count, which is what the printed line asks for) and line 14 = line 1 — the whole credit for other dependents must be taken nonrefundably, which is correct. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE by the printed "-0-" floor; whole dollars, rounded at this printed worksheet line per the round-at-the-printed-line convention (a no-op in practice — both operands are already Round-wrapped whole dollars).

Fact.Name: Credit Limit Worksheet B line 15 (the total the four bridge credits return to Worksheet A)
Fact.Description:
Worksheet B line 15 = "Enter the total of the amounts from — Schedule 3, line 5a; Schedule 3, line 6c; Schedule 3, line 6g; and Schedule 3, line 6h", with the marginal direction "Enter this amount on line 4 of Credit Limit Worksheet A" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 6). It is the second half of this node's obligation: the contract was named for line 14 but spans lines 14 AND 15, and a build that stopped at line 14 would have built the substitution without the feedback that makes it a credit ORDERING rather than a giveaway.
THE THREE ADDENDS ARE THE TWINS, READ THROUGH schedule3's Worksheet-B pass-throughs, never the public Schedule 3 lines. This is the load-bearing wiring rule of the whole build. The public /sched3Line5a, /sched3Line6c and /sched3Line6g read the public credit SELECTORS, whose plain arms read /totalCtcAndOdc — and /totalCtcAndOdc reads /sched8812CreditLimit, which reads this fact. One public reference here restores the cycle (/sched8812CreditLimit -> 5a -> /form5695CreditLimitWorksheetLine2 -> /totalCtcAndOdc -> /sched8812CreditLimit) that the original contract described, and because Switch construction is all-branch the dictionary would simply stop loading at 0% CPU with no error. It is also the tax-correct choice: line 15 asks for the amounts THIS filer figures, and this filer figures all four credits against worksheet line 14.
THE FOURTH ADDEND is schedule3:/worksheetBLine15DcHomebuyerTerm (dictionary/ty2025/form8859.xml) — the Worksheet-B TWIN, like the other three. Form 8859 also supplies limb 1 of /isCompletingCreditLimitWorksheetB, so a filer whose ONLY Worksheet-B credit is Form 8859 is both detected (routed to Worksheet B) and credited (the addend reaches line 15); leaving either half undone would leave such a filer detected but un-credited, or credited but undetected. tests/nodes/ty2025/form8859/wsb-8859-joins-worksheet-b-line-15 measures the addend half (line 15 1,600 -> 2,600, the CTC/ODC 5,695 -> 4,695) and -only-worksheet-b-credit-triggers-worksheet-b measures the trigger half. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (a total of nonrefundable credits); whole dollars, where the three addends already put them.

Fact.Name: Income from Puerto Rico excluded under section 933 (intake)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Schedule 8812 line 2a entry: "Enter income from Puerto Rico that you excluded" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s8.pdf, page 1). The exclusion is IRC 933(1), which exempts, for "an individual who is a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico during the entire taxable year, income derived from sources within Puerto Rico (except amounts received for services performed as an employee of the United States or any agency thereof)" (26 U.S.C. 933, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section933&num=0&edition=2024, the left column of a two-column extraction).
THE INTAKE HALF of the trio idiom, and NO shipping fact reads it directly; everything reads /puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933 below. A bare unanswered Writable inside the MAGI chain would take /dependentCreditMagi Incomplete by contagion for every filer in the corpus — the /aotcMagi failure class and the same reason /writableIsBonaFidePuertoRicoResident is never read directly either.
AN ENTRY, NOT A COMPUTATION. Nothing here sources income to Puerto Rico, applies the section 937(a) residence test or removes the US-government-employee carve-out; this writable accepts the figure the taxpayer put on line 2a and enforces only non-negativity. It is also NOT derived from /isBonaFidePuertoRicoResident and does not derive it: residency is a status Schedule 8812 Part II-B reads on its own for a filer with no PR-source income at all, and an excluded dollar must not imply a residency the filer never asserted. Both facts exist; one is not the other.
Optional - unanswered gives /puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933 $0, or the W-2 wages keyed as Puerto Rico source when there are any. Those keyed wages are already part of line 2a: this entry is the whole line, and the line is never smaller than the keyed wages.

The IsComplete/Switch guard idiom, the same shape as /isBonaFidePuertoRicoResident above and form2555 /form2555Line36HousingExclusion. $0 when unanswered UNDER-states MAGI, which is the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction on a phaseout — the reason /knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion below exists rather than a different tail. The taxpayer who has such income and is never asked is protected by the knockout, not by the tail, exactly as form2555's four entry aliases are.
CONSUMERS. /sched8812Line2dTotalExcludedIncome below (Schedule 8812 line 2d, which reaches line 3 and is therefore the section 24(b)(1) MAGI), and the knockout. THE SIX OTHER MAGI surfaces that section 24(b)(1)'s sibling statutes point at ARE WIRED to this path: form8863.xml:94, socialSecurity.xml:1669, form8839.xml:673, cleanVehicleCreditRepayment.xml:204, scheduleA.xml:3828, schedule1A.xml:39. A SEVENTH is taxCalculations:/magiForStudentLoanInterestDeduction, the section 221(b)(2)(C) MAGI, at taxCalculations.xml:373. The seven surfaces read the exclusions directly, so this fact's own retirement trigger below is the live record of what the knockout is still for, and condition (A) there is CLOSED. Nothing in this paragraph is a reason to keep the knockout any more.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Form 4563 line 15 — income excluded under section 931 (intake)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's Schedule 8812 line 2c entry: "Enter the amount from line 15 of your Form 4563" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s8.pdf, page 1). Form 4563 line 15 is "Add lines 7 through 14. This is the amount you may exclude from your gross income this tax year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4563.pdf, page 1) on the form captioned "Exclusion of Income for Bona Fide Residents of American Samoa" (line 1-2). The exclusion is IRC 931(a): "In the case of an individual who is a bona fide resident of a specified possession during the entire taxable year, gross income shall not include - (1) income derived from sources within any specified possession, and (2) income effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business by such individual within any specified possession", where "specified possession" means "Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands" (26 U.S.C. 931, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section931&num=0&edition=2024, the left column of a two-column extraction).
WHY THE PATH SAYS 931 AND THE FORM SAYS AMERICAN SAMOA. Section 931 covers three specified possessions; Form 4563 is the only one of them with a filing form attached to a Form 1040, because a bona fide resident of Guam or the CNMI files with the possession rather than with the United States. Schedule 8812 line 2c therefore names Form 4563 alone, and this entry is the section 931 term for every purpose the schedule has.
AN ENTRY, NOT A COMPUTATION: nothing here applies the section 937(a) residence test, sources income to a possession, or enforces the section 931(d) US-employee carve-out. Non-negativity is the only check.
Optional - unanswered gives /possessionIncomeExclusion931 $0.

Fact.Name: Income excluded under section 931 (Schedule 8812 line 2c), complete-safe
Fact.Description:
Schedule 8812 line 2c / Form 4563 line 15. THREE ARMS, in this order: the COMPUTED line 15 total /form4563Line15TotalExclusion whenever /form4563Part2ComponentLinesAnswered says the filer answered any of the eight Part II component lines; else the filer typed line 15 attestation /writablePossessionIncomeExclusion931 when answered, but never less than the computed total, which on that arm is the W-2 box 1 wages keyed to line 7; else the computed total, which is those keyed wages or $0.
THE ATTESTATION IS KEPT AS THE FALLBACK, not retired, and the predicate in front of it is a real "was the source answered" test rather than IsComplete on the computed total. That distinction is the whole design: /form4563Line15TotalExclusion is complete safe, so IsComplete on it is true on every return, and using it as the switch would silently override a filer who typed a line 15 and never saw Part II. Precedent: scheduleE /farmRentalNetIncome behind form4835 /form4835IncomeLinesAnswered.
NO COMMITTED SCENARIO MOVES: every scenario that carries this exclusion sets the line 15 intake and leaves all eight component lines blank, so the first arm is false and the second arm returns exactly what the superseded body returned.
The IsComplete/Switch guard idiom. Same $0 tail and same direction as /puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933 above: unanswered UNDER-states MAGI, taxpayer-favourable on a phaseout, and the protection is /knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion below rather than the tail.
A SEPARATE PATH FROM THE SECTION 933 SIBLING, never one conflated Dollar, and separate again from the section 911 figures. The consumer sets differ: Form 8960 line 13, Form 2441 lines 4/5, the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet line 2a and section 32(c)(1)(C) all read section 911 BY NAME and must never see this amount — form8960 /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback says so on its own face.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Schedule 8812 line 2b — the amounts from Form 2555 lines 45 and 50
Fact.Description:
Schedule 8812 line 2b, "Enter the amounts from lines 45 and 50 of your Form 2555" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s8.pdf, page 1) = form2555 /form2555Lines45And50ForeignEarnedIncomeTaxWorksheetLine2a when form2555 /filesForm2555ForeignEarnedIncomeExclusion is true, else $0. See the block banner above for why the figure is lines 45+50 and not the line-43 composite the contracts named.
GATED, for the same reason form8960 /niitMagiForeignEarnedIncomeAddback is gated and it is not belt-and-braces. The Form 2555 amount aliases are ungated; only the two Schedule 1 legs that carry the exclusion OUT of AGI are gated on the attestation. A filer who enters Form 2555 figures without answering the attestation therefore has an unreduced AGI, and adding 45+50 back to it would invent income. With the gate, the subtraction and the add-back cover exactly the same population and cancel to the pre-exclusion AGI, which is what section 24(b)(1) asks for.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents. NO FLOOR, deliberately: form2555 /form2555Line45ExclusionsNetOfAllocableDeductions has none either (Form 2555 line 45 prints no "if zero or less" instruction), so a filer whose line 44 exceeds their line 43 carries a negative line 45, a POSITIVE Schedule 1 line 8d, and the matching negative here. Flooring only this end would break the cancellation the paragraph above rests on. The obvious objection - that Schedule 8812 line 2b prints no parentheses and so cannot be meant to go negative - is unreachable in a filable return anyway: a non-zero line 2b requires the Form 2555 attestation to be TRUE, and form2555 /knockoutFilesForm2555 refuses every return that answers it true. If that knockout ever retires, this is the arm to re-examine.

Fact.Name: Schedule 8812 line 2d — add lines 2a through 2c
Fact.Description:
Schedule 8812 line 2d, "Add lines 2a through 2c" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s8.pdf, page 1) = the section 933 Puerto Rico exclusion, the Form 2555 lines 45+50 figure and the Form 4563 line 15 possession exclusion, summed. This is the whole of the section 24(b)(1) modification: "adjusted gross income increased by any amount excluded from gross income under section 911, 931, or 933" (26 U.S.C. 24, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section24&num=0&edition=2024), one term per statute in the order the statute names them, which is also the order the schedule prints them in.
ROUNDED HERE so that /dependentCreditMagi stays whole after the addition, matching the Round(/agi) it already applied.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, whole dollars. Normally non-negative; it can go negative only through line 2b's unfloored Form 2555 line-45 leg, which mirrors an equally positive Schedule 1 line 8d.

Fact.Name: The Publication 570 fraction has a denominator it can actually divide by
Fact.Description:
TRUE when income:/writableGrossIncomeFromAllSources is both ANSWERED and greater than zero. A KNOCKOUT INPUT and nothing else: it feeds /knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion below. It changes no deduction, and it is deliberately NOT wired into any apportionment site — every one of those already carries its own copy of this guard, and re-pointing them would be a behaviour change dressed as a refactor.
WHY THIS IS THE FIRST THING A RETIRING KNOCKOUT MUST TEST. Publication 570 chapter 4's whole apportionment is one fraction, "Gross income subject to U.S. income tax / Gross income from all sources (including excluded territory income)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, page 33, the LEFT column of a two-column extraction), and its denominator is NOT DERIVABLE from anything this graph holds — see income:/writableGrossIncomeFromAllSources, which records why /totalIncome cannot stand in. So the denominator is an ATTESTED optional intake with an unanswered tail, and that tail is the full-deduction arm at EVERY consumer: standardDeduction:/standardDeduction, scheduleA:/allowableStateLocalTaxes and its medical, mortgage and four charitable siblings, schedule1A:/allowableQualifiedCarLoanInterestDeduction, and taxCalculations:/allowableAdjustmentsToIncome. A section 933 filer who is never asked the denominator therefore gets the ENTIRE Publication 570 apportionment build inert: full standard deduction, unreduced itemized deductions, unreduced adjustments — every one of them in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction, and silently. That is a single condition covering every apportionment site at once, which is why it is tested here rather than site by site.
THE UNANSWERED TAIL IS NOT A BUG AT THOSE SITES and this fact is not a criticism of them: it is what keeps every committed return byte-identical, and it is the right default for the overwhelming majority of filers who exclude nothing. It is wrong only for the population this knockout screens, so the screen is where it belongs.
GREATER THAN ZERO, NOT MERELY ANSWERED, because a $0 denominator makes the fraction a division by zero rather than a small share. Same test the shipping consumers already make — standardDeduction:/pdfStandardDeductionModifiedForPossessionExclusion is the closest twin and uses the identical IsComplete-plus-GreaterThan pair.
COMPLETE ON EVERY RETURN BY CONSTRUCTION: IsComplete never propagates incompleteness, and the GreaterThan sits beside it inside an All, which is the shipping idiom at that twin. It resolves FALSE on every return that never answers the intake — which is every committed scenario, and the reason this fact's arrival moves no committed value.

FIRES WHEN the return has at least one child tax credit qualifying child (/ctcEligibleDependents above zero) and at least one Form 499R-2/W-2PR shows box 21 or box 23 above zero (/anyForm499R2W2PrShowsSocialSecurityOrMedicareTaxWithheld). Both legs are complete-safe, so an unanswered collection or dependents section does not fire it.
WHY IT REFUSES. Schedule 8812 line 21 is the social security, Medicare and Additional Medicare tax withheld, and its worksheet adds Form 499R-2/W-2PR boxes 21 and 23 to Form W-2 boxes 4 and 6. /sched8812Line21 reads Form W-2 only. Line 21 feeds Part II-B (a short line 21 under-states the additional child tax credit) and Credit Limit Worksheet B line 7 (a short line 21 over-states the credit limit, so the nonrefundable credit is over-claimed): the return would be wrong in one direction or the other. Adding the two boxes alone is not the fix: the worksheet's line 5 subtracts Form 8959 line 22, which reads Form W-2 only, so any Additional Medicare Tax inside box 23 would be added and never taken back out.

A possession return on which none of these holds is not refused and computes. The seven sibling MAGI surfaces read both exclusions directly.

Fact.Name: Modified AGI for purposes of dependent credits
Fact.Description:
Modified AGI for purposes of dependent credits. Reported on line 3 of Schedule 8812, "Add lines 1 and 2d" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s8.pdf, page 1), and named as the CTC/ODC MAGI by the instructions in as many words: "Modified AGI. For purposes of the CTC and ODC, your modified AGI is the amount on line 3 of Schedule 8812" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 2).
= Round(taxCalculations /agi) + /sched8812Line2dTotalExcludedIncome. Line 2a is /puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933, line 2b is /sched8812Line2bForm2555Exclusions and line 2c is /possessionIncomeExclusion931, and the sum of the three is line 2d. The Round on the AGI term is untouched, and the line-2d total is rounded at its own fact, so a return that answers none of the three entries produces exactly the AGI figure.
DIRECTION OF THE THREE $0 TAILS: a missing exclusion UNDER-states MAGI, which SHRINKS the section 24(b)(2) phaseout and OVER-claims the credit - taxpayer-favourable, i.e. the non-conservative direction. That is why /knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion refuses a return with a possession entry the other six MAGI surfaces cannot see, and why form2555 /knockoutFilesForm2555 refuses the section 911 population outright.

Fact.Name: Display value for PDF Schedule 8812, Line 24
Fact.Description:
Printed Schedule 8812 line 24 if completing Part II-B; undefined otherwise.
THE PRINTED LINE IS A SUM OF TWO AMOUNTS, NOT ONE. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s8.pdf, page 2, verbatim: "1040 and 1040-SR filers: Enter the total of the amounts from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 27a, and Schedule 3 (Form 1040), line 11. 1040-NR filers: Enter the amount from Schedule 3 (Form 1040), line 11." Form 1040 line 27a is the earned income credit, eitc:/earnedIncomeCredit; Schedule 3 line 11 is the excess social security and tier 1 RRTA tax withheld, schedule3:/excessSocialSecurityTaxWithheld. Reading the earned income credit alone would leave the printed Part II-B not footing on its own face for any filer with excess social security withheld: line 23 minus the printed line 24 would not equal the printed line 25.
PRINT ONLY AND NO DOUBLE COUNT, which is why this is a display correction and not a tax movement. No derived fact reads this one - line 25 is /pdf8812Line25, which reads /socialSecurityOverEitc, and that fact already subtracts BOTH terms inline in its own Subtrahends (eitc:/earnedIncomeCredit and schedule3:/excessSocialSecurityTaxWithheld). So line 25 was already the printed line 25; only the line-24 box was short a leg, and adding it makes the two boxes foot without changing line 25, line 26, line 27 or any dollar on Form 1040. Both addends are total on every return that reaches Part II-B: line 25 reads each of them unwrapped today, so neither needs a complete-safe wrapper here.
THE 1040-NR ARM IS NOT A SEPARATE ARM. On a Form 1040-NR return the earned income credit is unavailable and eitc:/earnedIncomeCredit is $0, so the same Add prints the 1040-NR line (Schedule 3 line 11 alone) without a branch.

═══ THE SHAPE, per the project owner's direction to "resolve the Form 4563 possession-income conflict in the audit's preferred shape": THE DECISION IS THE PER INCOME TYPE SHAPE FOR THE INCOME SIDE, and the reason is that the contract's two candidate shapes are not two shapes of ONE quantity: they are two different quantities its prose ran together.
WHAT THE CONTRACT SAYS. Replacing /knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion needs a collection keyed per income item (which Schedule K-1, which Schedule F, which employer), which is not built. Its round-5 RECONCILED paragraph set that Shape A beside the Shape B this fact sums, said one-quantity-one-fact prefers Shape A, and referred the call out because 34 promoted facts ride on it.
WHY THE EIGHT TYPED SCALARS ARE THE RIGHT INCOME SIDE, read off the form rather than chosen for convenience. Form 4563 Part II IS per income TYPE on its own face: lines 7 through 14 are wages, taxable interest, ordinary dividends, business income, capital gain, rental real estate and royalties, farm income and other income, and line 15 adds them (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4563.pdf, page 1 through 46). The eight intakes are that printed list one for one, and the eight OrZero wrappers above are its eight boxes. A per item collection would still have to print these eight boxes, so it would be a SECOND home for the same dollars rather than a better home for them.
WHY A COLLECTION IN THIS MODULE WOULD BE THE WRONG PLACE FOR THE PER ITEM QUESTION, which is the half of the ShapeNote that is right about the world. The graph already HAS a per item possession-source convention and it lives on the ITEM, in the item's own module: scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/writableExcludedTerritoryNetProfit. scheduleSE:/possessionUntreatedNonScheduleCSelfEmployment names the two twins that are missing by name, a per Schedule K-1 box 14 code A amount and a per Schedule F amount, and those belong to scheduleE and scheduleF. A third home for per item possession amounts, sitting in ctcOdc, is exactly the pathology the same audit condemns for the section 179 election two rows above this one.
THE TWO CONDITIONS THE CONTRACT SAID THESE SCALARS CANNOT REACH, ANSWERED ON THE SOURCES RATHER THAN CONCEDED. Condition (ii), the prior year charitable carryover, does NOT need items at all: 26 CFR 1.861-8(e)(12)(i) apportions the section 170 deduction "on the basis of the relative amounts of gross income" (26 CFR 1.861-8, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-26/section-1.861-8 through 1050, quoted in full on scheduleA:/possessionUnapportionedCharitableCarryover), which is the RETURN LEVEL Publication 570 chapter 4 fraction that already ships and that /possessionApportionmentDenominatorUsable above already guards. What is missing is a scheduleA computation multiplying the thirteen carryover facts by that fraction, and NO shape of intake in this module supplies it. Condition (vi) DOES need a per item answer, and the paragraph above says whose module owns it. So neither shape discharges either condition from this file: the collection would have cost a build and bought no narrowing.
THE DIVERGENCE THE CONTRACT ASKED TO HAVE DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT SILENT, in its own words, "if they stay, conditions (ii) and (vi) need an explicitly disclosed divergence rather than silence". THE EIGHT SCALARS ARE THE FORM 4563 INCOME SIDE AND NOTHING ELSE. Measured by grepping the module for each of the eight names: every one is read by its own OrZero wrapper and by /form4563Part2ComponentLinesAnswered, and by nothing else in the dictionary. They apportion no deduction, they source no income ITEM, and they are not the deduction side of section 931(b) or section 933(1).
THE DEDUCTION SIDE IS UNBUILT IN TWO HALVES AND THIS FACT DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. The "not definitely related" half is the Publication 570 fraction, built at six consumer sites and missing only the carryover (condition (ii)). The "definitely related" half has NO fact anywhere in the dictionary: Publication 570 chapter 4, "Deductions that specifically apply to your excluded territory income are not allowable on your U.S. income tax return" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, page 32 through 2257, the RIGHT column of a two column extraction), which Form 4563's own instructions print as "Deductions and credits you cannot take on Form 1040 or 1040-SR. If you claim the exclusion, you cannot take any deduction or credit on your tax return that is definitely related to the excluded income" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4563.pdf, page 2 through 91, RIGHT column). The section 911 sibling shows the shape such an intake takes when it is built: form2555:/writableForm2555Line44DeductionsAllocableToExcludedIncome. NOTHING IS MINTED FOR IT HERE, deliberately: every consumer that would read it lives in another module, and a writable with no consumer is the debt this closeout exists to retire, not to add to.
THE KNOCKOUT IS UNTOUCHED. /knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion below keeps all six conditions and both wirings. Nothing here narrows it. ═══
